name: arch linux
descriptionfull: Arch Linux is a lightweight, rolling-release distribution for experienced users who want full control. It ships a minimal base system, so you install only the components you need.

name: tiny core linux
description: An ultra-light distro that runs entirely from RAM
descriptionfull: Tiny Core Linux is a minimalist, modular distribution with a very small download. It boots entirely into RAM, running fast even on old hardware, and you add software on demand as extensions.

name: linux mint
description: A friendly, polished distro for beginners
descriptionfull: Linux Mint is an Ubuntu-based distribution focused on being familiar and easy to use. Its Cinnamon desktop has a traditional layout, and multimedia codecs work out of the box.

name: ubuntu
descriptionfull: Ubuntu LTS is a Debian-based distribution backed by Canonical, with a huge community and extensive documentation. Its long-term support releases get multi-year updates and ship with GNOME.

name: debian
description: A rock-solid, stable universal operating system
descriptionfull: Debian is one of the oldest and most influential distributions, known for stability and a strong commitment to free software. This small netinst image downloads the rest of the system during installation, so it needs an internet connection.

name: fedora workstation
description: A modern distro with cutting-edge software
descriptionfull: Fedora Workstation is a community distribution sponsored by Red Hat that ships recent software while staying stable. It uses GNOME by default and is a popular choice for developers.

name: manjaro
description: Arch Linux made easy for everyday users
descriptionfull: Manjaro is built on Arch Linux but adds a graphical installer, automatic hardware detection and curated update branches. This KDE Plasma edition gives you Arch's rolling releases without the manual setup.

name: opensuse leap
description: A stable, enterprise-grade release with long support
descriptionfull: openSUSE Leap is a fixed-release distribution built on the same sources as SUSE Linux Enterprise, with 24 months of updates per release. It uses the Agama installer and is a dependable choice for desktops and servers. This is the offline installer, so it needs no internet connection during installation.

name: kali linux
description: A security-focused distro for penetration testing
descriptionfull: Kali Linux is a Debian-based distribution packed with hundreds of tools for security research, penetration testing and digital forensics. It is meant for professionals and learners, not as a daily desktop.

name: alpine linux
description: A tiny, security-oriented distro for containers
descriptionfull: Alpine Linux is built around musl libc and BusyBox, giving it a very small footprint of a few hundred megabytes. It is a favorite base for Docker images, routers and lightweight servers.

name: nixos
description: A declarative distro configured with code
descriptionfull: NixOS lets you describe your entire system in a single configuration file, making setups reproducible and easy to roll back. It is ideal for people who like treating their OS like code.
